correctness.rationale: Banerjee–Ghosh Dastidar Theorem 1.5 supplies only the underlying exact odd-index support predicate 3n-1=epsilon*p^(4k+1)*square and Kronecker(-2/p)=-1. From M=(3n-1)/2 the two disjoint prime-square types have prime residues 7/13 and 5/23 mod24; n mod8 splits according to u parity. Every admissible M has a unique odd-exponent prime p, avoiding overcount. Higher k and p|u contribute O(sqrt X). Fixed-modulus PNT with a uniform logarithmic expansion for u<=Y^(1/8), combined with summable u^-2 log^j u moments and the Y^(7/8) tail, establishes the two-term and all-logarithmic-orders formula. Euler-product differentiation yields S_odd=2ζ(2)/3, S_even=2ζ(2)/9 and the log moments producing delta ratios. Independent GF mod4 1..2400 equals prime-square support (322 indices); no asymptotic inference from finite counts.

limitations: Odd indices only, congruence 2 mod4 only; big-O does not yield explicit finite crossover X; PNT external input is classical.
